record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.context_brief: Existence of nonzero traces on L^{WEYL}_{1,∞}.
record.original_question: Show that the Weyl-number ideal L^{WEYL}_{1,\infty} supports at least one non-vanishing trace. The source explicitly singles this out as the author's personal favourite and suggests that such traces may even be singular and spectral.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a complex Banach space and $T: X \to X$ a bounded linear operator. For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, define the $n$-th Weyl number of $T$ by
$$x_n(T) := \sup\{ a_n(TA) : A: \ell_2 \to X,\ \|A\| \le 1\},$$
where $a_n$ denotes the $n$-th approximation number, $a_n(S) = \inf\{\|S - F\| : F\text{ finite rank},\ \mathrm{rank}(F) < n\}$.

Let $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$ be the operator ideal consisting of all operators $T$ between arbitrary Banach spaces such that
$$\sup_{n \ge 1} n \cdot x_n(T) < \infty,$$
viewed as a two-sided ideal in the class of all bounded operators between Banach spaces.

A trace on $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ defined on the components $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}(X,X)$ for every Banach space $X$, satisfying the commutator property $\tau(AB) = \tau(BA)$ whenever $AB$ and $BA$ both lie in the ideal, and which is unitarily/ideal invariant in the usual sense.

Problem: Prove or disprove that there exists a nonzero trace on $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was located. The question of whether the Weyl-number Lorentz ideal $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$ admits a nonzero (and possibly singular, spectral) trace is stated as an outstanding open problem in the operator-ideal literature, with no subsequent paper found announcing a solution.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Weyl inequality in Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Weyl numbers, defined by Pietsch, are truly important in the study of Riesz operators in Banach spaces and yield optimal eigenvalue asymptotics.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms standard definition and central role of Weyl numbers, but provides no construction of a nonzero trace on the (1,∞)-Weyl ideal.
